sections.category: Anthropic publishes Claude containment architecture: gVisor, Seatbelt/Bubblewrap, and per-OS VMs

bullets.body: Anthropic's engineering team published a detailed post titled "How we contain Claude across products" on the official engineering blog, walking through the agent-isolation stack it has converged on for each product: a gVisor container with seccomp syscall filtering on isolated infrastructure for Claude.ai (ephemeral per-session filesystems, minimal blast radius), OS-native process sandboxes for Claude Code (Seatbelt on macOS, Bubblewrap on Linux — the team reports an 84% reduction in permission prompts after delegating command approvals to a model-based classifier), and full guest VMs for Claude Cowork running on Apple's Virtualization framework on macOS and HCS on Windows, with credentials held on the host and files mounted into the VM under read-only, read-write, or read-write-no-delete modes, per [Anthropic Engineering](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/how-we-contain-claude). The post argues that "the software you build yourself is often the weakest" component and that mature hypervisors and container runtimes outperform custom security wrappers Anthropic had developed around them. Simon Willison amplified the publication late Saturday evening and demonstrated the new posture in practice the same weekend by getting Claude Opus 4.8 (in Claude Code for web) to refactor Datasette Lite from Web Workers to service workers so Python ASGI apps now execute server-side responses inside the browser via Pyodide, shipping a working FastCGI demo and a Datasette 1.0a31 demo built fully under the sandboxed agent — per [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/May/30/how-we-contain-claude/) and his [Pyodide ASGI research note](https://simonwillison.net/2026/May/30/pyodide-asgi-browser/).

sections.category: Snowflake heads into Summit 26 with $6B AWS Graviton commit, intent to acquire Natoma for MCP identity, and a +44% two-day stock rip

bullets.body: Snowflake stacked three pre-Summit catalysts inside the May 27-29 window that have reset the Summit-26 narrative going into Monday's keynote: a $6 billion five-year commitment to AWS that expands Snowflake's use of Amazon's Graviton general-purpose chips and cloud GPUs for agentic AI workloads — 2.4x larger than the 2023 AWS commitment — per the [Snowflake-AWS press release](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/snowflake-expands-aws-collaboration-with-6b-commitment-to-accelerate-enterprise-agentic-ai-adoption/) and [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/snowflake-aws-6bn-graviton-ai-commitment); a definitive agreement to acquire Natoma, an enterprise Model Context Protocol gateway that enforces identity, policy, and audit at the individual MCP tool-call level so Snowflake can govern which AI agents can invoke which downstream systems, per the [Natoma press release](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/snowflake-announces-intent-to-acquire-natoma-providing-secure-connectivity-for-the-agentic-enterprise/) and [CIO Dive](https://www.ciodive.com/news/snowflake-targets-ai-agent-adoption-aws/821393/); and a Q1 FY27 earnings beat (adjusted EPS $0.39 vs $0.32 consensus on $1.39B revenue, +33% YoY) with raised full-year product-revenue guidance to 31%, per [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/05/27/snowflakes-stock-surges-hours-solid-earnings-beat-multibillion-dollar-aws-cloud-deal/). SNOW gapped up 36% Thursday on the print and added another 6.88% Friday to close near $255, the largest two-day rally in the stock's public history. Online registration for Summit 26 closes today Sunday May 31, with the Monday June 1 5:00 PM PT opening keynote pairing CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei in front of a projected 20,000+ in-person attendees.

sections.category: CNN files first-by-a-TV-network copyright suit against Perplexity; OpenAI publishes Frontier Governance Framework as EU Aug-2 deadline closes in

bullets.body: Two state-changes in the past 72 hours have crystallized the multi-front regulatory pressure that will follow AI vendors into the June conference cycle. Thursday May 28, CNN filed a 54-page copyright complaint against Perplexity AI in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleging the AI search company scraped and redistributed more than 17,000 CNN stories, photos, and videos after a 2025 licensing deal fell through and Perplexity ignored a follow-up cease-and-desist — this is CNN's first AI copyright action and the first by any TV network. Perplexity Chief Communications Officer Jesse Dwyer responded that "you can't copyright facts," per [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/05/28/cnn-sues-perplexity-alleging-massive-copyright-infringement/) and [Variety](https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/cnn-sues-perplexity-alleging-copyright-infringement-1236760987/). Perplexity now faces nine active publisher suits with the addition of CNN. The same day, OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework explicitly mapping internal Preparedness Framework controls to the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI and California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act, ahead of the EU's August 2, 2026 full-enforceability date — a [TechTimes Sunday analysis](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317461/20260531/ai-regulation-2026-opens-three-fronts-cnn-sues-perplexity-openai-aligns-eu-rules.htm) dated May 31 frames the three fronts (litigation-driven copyright costs, DOJ-led federalism preemption against state AI laws including the May 14 Colorado SB 26-189 successor statute, and EU-led disclosure infrastructure) as producing distinct non-transferable obligations that vendors cannot resolve under a single compliance strategy. Separately, Sam Altman walked back his 2023 "jobs apocalypse" rhetoric at a virtual CBA conference appearance in Sydney, conceding he was "pretty wrong" about the entry-level white-collar elimination he had expected from ChatGPT-era AI, per [Cyprus Mail](https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/05/31/openais-altman-says-ai-unlikely-to-lead-to-jobs-apocalypse).

sections.category: Unsloth ships v0.1.43-beta with CUDA 13.3 + restored Apple Silicon llama.cpp binaries; PyPI bump to 2026.5.9 on Sunday

bullets.body: Unsloth pushed two Sunday-morning release artifacts that together close the local-fine-tuning gap left by the v0.1.42-beta API-calling drop on Tuesday May 26. The core `unsloth` Python package jumped to 2026.5.9 on PyPI today May 31 (preceded by 2026.5.8 on May 26), and the companion `unsloth-zoo` utility package bumped to 2026.5.5 the same day, per [unsloth on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/unsloth/) and [unsloth-zoo on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/unsloth-zoo/). The matching Unsloth Studio tag, v0.1.43-beta, lands CUDA 13.3 support with prebuilt `llama.cpp` binaries for Windows — explicitly resolving the "gibberish output" problem operators have been reporting under CUDA 13.2 — and restores Apple Silicon M1-M4 support for macOS 14, 15, and 26 with prebuilt binaries after a previous regression had forced Mac users onto source builds; Blackwell GPU support remains held pending an upstream CUDA compatibility fix. The v0.1.42-beta foundation from earlier in the week (May 26) had already added OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API calling with auto prompt caching for 50-90% cost savings, external inference backend connections to vLLM, Ollama, and llama-server, and proper Japanese/Chinese/Indian-language tokenization on the chat side. The cumulative effect: a single open-source fine-tuning stack that now spans Apple Silicon laptops, consumer NVIDIA cards under CUDA 13.3, and external API providers behind the same UI — the broadest hardware coverage Unsloth has shipped in one release window. The companion Hugging Face training-hub posts continue the weekday-cadence router-only LoRA documentation, with the May 28 release post for v2026.5.8 having already shipped TRL v0.16.0 drop-in compatibility and the Kimi K3-Pro 218B MoE port, per [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/blog/unsloth-trl-v0-16-0-joint-selective-expert-checkpoint-costa-huang-rlhf-pipeline-drop-in-compatibility-may-28-2026).

sections.category: Bay Area June-July calendar: Snowflake Summit 26 online registration closes today, Summit opens tomorrow; Microsoft Build, WWDC, Databricks, and AI Engineer World's Fair line up across the next five weeks

bullets.body: The Bay Area conference window opens at 5:00 PM PT tomorrow Monday June 1 — online registration for Snowflake Summit 26 closes today Sunday May 31, with full-conference passes at $2,295, and the opening keynote pairs CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei in front of a projected 20,000+ in-person attendees at Moscone Center across Monday-Thursday June 1-4, per [Snowflake Summit 26](https://www.snowflake.com/en/summit/) and the [Snowflake Summit 26 FAQ](https://www.snowflake.com/en/summit/faq/). Microsoft Build 2026 runs Tuesday-Wednesday June 2-3 at Fort Mason Center San Francisco with Satya Nadella's opening keynote and the Windows Agent Framework slated for open-source MIT-licensed release, free online stream with in-person passes via the [session catalog](https://www.thurrott.com/microsoft/334704/microsofts-build-2026-session-catalog-is-now-live). Apple WWDC26 runs Monday-Friday June 8-12 with the keynote Monday June 8 at 10:00 AM PT and an Apple Park in-person event open to registered developers via random lottery, per [Apple Developer WWDC26](https://developer.apple.com/wwdc26/). AI Tinkerers SF hosts its invite-only VIP Dinner: Harnessing Agents on Tuesday June 2 for a hand-selected cohort of engineers shipping agentic systems into production, per [AI Tinkerers SF](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/p/ai-tinkerers-vip-dinner-harnessing-agents), with a Voice Agents Science Fair sponsored by ElevenLabs separately scheduled in June per the [AI Tinkerers SF events page](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/events). Databricks Data + AI Summit runs Monday-Thursday June 15-18 across Moscone North, West, and South with 800+ sessions and named speakers from Databricks, Microsoft, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Anthropic, and LangChain per [Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/dataaisummit). AI Engineer World's Fair caps June into early July at Moscone West, Monday-Thursday June 29-July 2, with 250+ speakers across 20+ tracks, 50+ workshops, 6,000+ stated attendance, and discounted hotel group rates expiring June 6 (Parc 55 already sold out), per [AI Engineer World's Fair](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/2026). Looking further out: GitHub Universe returns to SF Fort Mason October 28-29 per the [GitHub Universe FAQ](https://githubuniverse.com/faq); AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas with registration opening June 16 per [AWS re:Invent](https://aws.amazon.com/events/reinvent/).
